description: Refactor core OpenClaw runtime so forward-facing agents are structurally unaware of OpenClaw internals, with strict core failure classification and explicit internal-to-user-safe mapping.

context.currentProblem: Forward-facing agents can still reason about runtime internals (gateway, toolset, internal tool IDs) and leak infrastructure language to users during failures.
context.desiredState: In platform runtime mode, the model only sees product-domain capabilities and product-safe outcomes. Internal runtime/tool errors are normalized at source and never exposed to model-facing or user-facing content.
context.architectureGoal: Replace direct internal-tool exposure with capability facade + adapter boundary normalization, strict canonical failure envelope, explicit mapping, and core recovery policy.

userStories.title: Define platform runtime contract
userStories.description: As a platform engineer, I need a locked runtime contract so implementation and migration happen against one unambiguous source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Architecture decision record defines `platform_agent` runtime mode and explicit boundaries
Contract specifies model-visible, internal-only, and user-visible data classes
Contract includes forbidden model-visible internal concepts (gateway, plugin, toolset, OpenClaw identity, internal tool IDs)
Contract includes compatibility notes for existing agents
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This story gates all implementation stories.

userStories.title: Add platform_agent runtime mode
userStories.description: As a runtime maintainer, I need a first-class mode switch so forward-facing agents run with platform-safe core behavior by design.
acceptanceCriteria: Agent runtime supports `platform_agent` mode in config and scope resolution
`platform_agent` mode is off by default for backward compatibility
Runtime mode can be enabled per agent (starting with Vibey)
Legacy mode behavior remains unchanged when flag is off
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Do not break existing non-platform agents.

userStories.title: Introduce product capability facade
userStories.description: As an agent-runtime architect, I need product-domain capabilities so the model no longer depends on internal tool identity.
acceptanceCriteria: Capability facade interface exists with product-domain request/response types
Model-facing tool surface resolves to capability IDs, not internal tool IDs
Capability metadata avoids infrastructure language
Capability facade supports current Vibey critical flows (create, update, publish path primitives)
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This is the core abstraction seam.

userStories.title: Implement internal adapter layer
userStories.description: As a runtime engineer, I need adapters so internal tools can still execute while staying hidden behind capability contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Adapters map capability requests to current internal tool calls
Adapters map internal tool results to capability results
No raw internal tool ID is returned to model-facing payloads in `platform_agent` mode
Adapter failures emit failure envelopes only (no raw internal message passthrough)
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Initial adapter coverage can focus on Vibey high-frequency capability set.

userStories.title: Add canonical failure envelope
userStories.description: As a runtime maintainer, I need one strict failure model so all recovery and user-safe messaging is deterministic.
acceptanceCriteria: Core enum exists with canonical classes: TRANSIENT, INPUT_INVALID, ACCESS_BLOCKED, CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, SYSTEM_FAULT
Failure envelope type includes class, retryable, retryBudget, userMessageKey, businessNextStepType, internalDebug
All adapter failures must return this envelope
No ad-hoc class names are used outside canonical enum
TypeScript compiles without errors

userStories.title: Build strict failure classifier
userStories.description: As a platform engineer, I need deterministic classification from internal errors to canonical classes so retries and mapping are reliable.
acceptanceCriteria: Classifier maps internal tool/runtime error signatures to canonical failure classes
Classifier returns deterministic output for the same input
Classifier populates retryability and retry budget fields
Classifier never emits user-visible raw internal error text
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Use table-driven mapping with explicit defaults.

userStories.title: Implement explicit internal-to-user-safe mapper
userStories.description: As a product platform owner, I need explicit mapped outcomes so users only receive business-safe guidance.
acceptanceCriteria: Mapper converts failure envelopes to user-safe outcomes with message key and action
Mapping table is explicit, versioned, and complete for all canonical failure classes
Mapped copy excludes infrastructure terms (gateway, plugin, toolset, OpenClaw, internal tool IDs)
Mapper does not allow fallback to raw internal text
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This is a core contract, not UI filtering.

userStories.title: Add core retry and fallback policy engine
userStories.description: As a runtime engineer, I need recovery orchestration before response construction so agent flow continues without infra-language leaks.
acceptanceCriteria: Retry engine uses failure envelope retry fields and bounded budget
Non-retryable failures skip retries deterministically
Fallback engine selects business-safe action (`continue`, `ask_input`, `defer`, `stop`) from mapped outcome
No infrastructure remediation instruction can be emitted by policy engine
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Recovery must happen before model-visible/user-visible payload assembly.

userStories.title: Enforce model context boundary in platform mode
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need hard context boundaries so the model cannot reason about engine internals.
acceptanceCriteria: System prompt/tool context builder excludes OpenClaw operational identity in `platform_agent` mode
Internal runtime controls and remediation instructions are excluded from model-visible context
Internal tool IDs are excluded from model-visible context
Soul/persona and product behavior guidance remain available
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Boundary should be structural; not only instruction text.

userStories.title: Refactor payload construction to consume safe outcomes only
userStories.description: As a runtime maintainer, I need payload assembly to consume only mapped safe outcomes so raw error leakage is impossible.
acceptanceCriteria: Payload builder reads mapped user-safe outcome objects only in `platform_agent` mode
Raw tool/runtime error strings cannot be inserted into assistant/user payload text
Mutating action failures still use mapped safe messaging (no raw exception passthrough)
Legacy mode behavior remains unchanged
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Core runtime behavior change; avoid upper-layer patch reliance.

userStories.title: Add observability without user leakage
userStories.description: As an operations engineer, I need internal diagnostics preserved for debugging while keeping user output safe.
acceptanceCriteria: Internal debug logs include envelope class, adapter source, retry attempts, and redacted internal details
Telemetry events separate internal diagnostics from user-facing message keys
No raw internal error text appears in user-facing event streams in `platform_agent` mode
Dashboards/queries can monitor class distribution and fallback rates
TypeScript compiles without errors

userStories.title: Migrate Vibey to platform_agent mode
userStories.description: As a product owner, I need Vibey moved to the new core runtime mode to eliminate infra-language behavior in production paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Vibey config enables `platform_agent` runtime mode behind feature flag
Vibey critical conversation flows run through capability facade and adapter boundary
Vibey does not receive internal tool IDs in model-visible context
Rollback path exists to legacy mode via config flag
TypeScript compiles without errors

userStories.title: Add forced-failure test matrix end-to-end
userStories.description: As a QA engineer, I need deterministic forced-failure tests so the new core contract is proven under real failure scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: Unit tests cover classifier and mapper completeness for all canonical classes
Integration tests inject internal failures (including `vibey_backend`) and verify envelope + mapped outcomes
E2E tests verify conversation output never includes `gateway`, `plugin`, `toolset`, `OpenClaw`, `vibey_backend`, `restart`
E2E tests verify flow continues or asks only business-relevant next step
TypeScript compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This is the release gate story.

userStories.title: Rollout and legacy-path decommission plan
userStories.description: As a platform lead, I need a controlled rollout and cleanup plan so regressions are contained and old leak-prone paths do not persist.
acceptanceCriteria: Staged rollout plan exists with explicit go/no-go metrics
Production rollout supports gradual enablement and fast rollback
Post-stabilization plan removes legacy direct-exposure path for forward-facing agents
Runbook documents incident response and rollback triggers
TypeScript compiles without errors
